notes:
FORMAT. Fragments are copied from the printed lines with the whitespace at each end removed. Inner spacing is kept. Marks give the run of asterisks as printed. Which year each asterisk belongs to depends on its column under the header "1879, '80, '81, '82." (columns 4/9/14/19). Trimming hides that, so here is how each row reads:
- 81, 82, 85, 100, 111: '79 '80 '81
- 83, 86, 93/94, 95, 96, 102, 103, 112, 113, 114: all four years
- 84, 87, 91, 110: '80 '81
- 90, 98, 101: '80 '81 '82. In row 90 the third asterisk sits one column right of the others (col 20), but it can only be the '82 column.
- 92, 99, 104: '79 '80
- 109, 115: '81 only
- 88, 89, 97, 105-108, 116-120: none
Heights are in "other" as printed. Only 81 and 91 print "ft."; the rest print a ditto mark (").

KEEPERS. A full stop ends the keeper's name in several rows ("J. Youngclause.", "D. McCulloch.", "Alx. McEachern.", "John Ewing.", "W. McLellan.", "A. Murray.", "W. Maill.", "Andrew Lyall.", "Ralph Ewing.", "Jas. Beggs.", "H. Morrison."). I took this as the row's closing punctuation and dropped it from the keeper entries. The fragments still have it. "Alex. Thompson" (83) is printed without one.
"John Ewing" is printed for both 95 Dhuheartach and 102 Skervuile. He might be one man who moved, two men with the same name, or a printing slip.

BRACES.
- 86 Monach Island: the braces group two heights (150 and 62, which suggests two lights). They are not a mark on the station, so they're in "other".
- 93 Hynish Signal Tower and 94 Skerryvore: a brace on the left joins them, so they share one set of asterisks. A second brace after the names joins them to one height (150 ") and one keeper (Alx. McEachern). These are printed only on 93's line. I put the keeper on 93 alone so he isn't counted twice in the roll. He should be read as serving the Hynish/Skerryvore pair, since Hynish was Skerryvore's shore station.
- 116-120: a right-hand brace gives "Isle of Man." (printed on 118's line) as the place for all five. I put that place on each of them and used "}" as their mark.

ISLE OF MAN STATIONS (116-120). In the print they still sit under the "Mainland, Skye, and Inner Hebrides" sub-heading, so that is the coast I gave them. The note right after the list says "The last five stations are now placed at the head of the W. of England stations under Mr. P. Kermode."

119. It is printed "119.-1880. Bahama Rock L.V.". I took "119" as the number and put "-1880." in other. Its meaning is unclear: maybe the vessel was listed or withdrawn in 1880, or a different station was numbered 119 before then.

PLACE / NAME SPLITS (my choices).
- 92 "Ardnamurchan, Pt. Argyle": name "Ardnamurchan, Pt.", place "Argyle".
- 95: the place "S. of Ross of Mull" wraps onto line 2297, and I joined the two parts with a space.
- 94: place given as "off Tyree".
- 97: place given as "Loch Eil".
- 106: place given as "Kintyre Sound".
- 96 Sound of Mull and 103 Rhinns of Islay: kept whole as names.

SPELLINGS KEPT AS PRINTED.
- "Sye" (89, Rona): almost certainly Skye.
- "Island Glass" (85): Eilean Glas.
- "Rosshire" (90).
- "Tyree" (93, 94).
- "Argyle" (92).
- "Chickens Rock" (118): Chicken Rock.
- "Longness" (120): Langness.
- "Lochindaul" (104): Loch Indaal.
- "Rhuvaal" (100): Rhuvaal / Rubh' a' Mhail.
- "Dhuheartach" (95): Dubh Artach.
- "W. Maill" (101): the surname may be a misprint.

No light characters are given in this list.
